column3: The Hebrew says “after Abimelech” without an explicit “the time of”.
The Hebrew uses “he” without repeating Tola and narrates his death as a separate clause.
The Hebrew actively says Jair arose after “him”; BSB names Tola and recasts the succession in a passive construction.
The Hebrew specifies young donkeys and actively says people call the towns Havvoth-jair; BSB uses “are called”.
The Hebrew joins the death and burial with “and”, rather than making the death a “when” clause.
The Hebrew says “in the eyes of the LORD” and repeats “the gods of” with each group; BSB condenses the repetitions.
The Hebrew repeats singular “in the hand” before both peoples and calls the Ammonites “the sons of Ammon”.
The Hebrew uses the collective singular “the Amorite”; BSB uses plural “Amorites”.
The Hebrew calls the Ammonites “the sons of Ammon”.
The Hebrew introduces the peoples with “from” in an elliptical question; BSB draws them into the following clause about oppression.
The Hebrew uses the names Amalek and Maon and singular “their hand”; BSB has plural peoples and “their hands”.
The Hebrew says “all that is good in Your eyes”; BSB condenses the image to “as You see fit”.
The Hebrew explicitly names His soul and describes it as becoming short in response to Israel’s suffering; BSB expresses this as being unable to bear it.
The Hebrew says the Ammonites were summoned without explicitly adding “to arms”.
The Hebrew explicitly asks who the man is who will begin fighting and calls the Ammonites “the sons of Ammon”.
